title: Evidence base for digital mental health therapeutics
bottleneck: Thousands of mental health apps exist but almost none have rigorous efficacy data, and the few FDA-authorized digital therapeutics show high dropout and modest effects. Engagement, not just content, is the unsolved problem: the people who need these tools most use them least.
why_it_blocks: Digital therapeutics are pitched as the answer to the access bottleneck, but without proven efficacy and engagement, they risk becoming a low-quality substitute that lets systems claim coverage without delivering care.
current_state: A handful of prescription digital therapeutics are authorized (e.g., for depression, insomnia, substance use) with payer coverage lagging. Research focuses on adaptive, AI-personalized interventions, but validation standards are unsettled. Prescription digital therapeutics have cleared FDA authorization for several conditions, yet reimbursement and clinician workflows have not caught up, limiting real-world adoption.
